QF.id: Evaluating Fund Performance and Fund Selection_36

question.text: Pooja is 55 years old and planning to retire at 60. For her NPS account, what is the qualitatively correct direction of her asset-allocation glide path as she nears retirement?

answer.text: Equity exposure should be increased while corporate bond and government securities exposure are reduced
Equity, corporate bond and government securities exposure should all be kept unchanged at their initial level
Equity exposure should be reduced while corporate bond and government securities exposure are increased
The entire corpus should be moved to 100% equity for maximum growth

explanation.text: The Logic: NISM Series XVII (Retirement Adviser, June 2025) p.111-113 and p.160 describe the NPS lifecycle funds (LC25/LC50/LC75) where, as the subscriber approaches retirement, equity (E) exposure is progressively reduced and corporate bonds (C) and government securities (G) exposure are correspondingly increased. At 55 with only 5 years to retirement, Pooja is moving from accumulation to capital-preservation, so option C captures the qualitatively correct glide path. The Trap: Option A reverses the glide path. Option B ignores the lifecycle de-risking entirely. Option D ignores the short time horizon. In the original ambiguous version a specific quantitative split (20/30/50) was keyed, but the source p.114-116 lifecycle tables at age 55-and-beyond show LC25 at 5/5/90, LC50 at 10/10/80, and LC75 at 15/10/75 - none of which equal 20/30/50 - so the specific split was not source-supported without specifying which lifecycle fund applied. Note: The original question was ambiguous because it asked for an exact allocation without specifying the LC25/LC50/LC75 choice, and the keyed 20/30/50 split is not on the source tables. The item has been rewritten as a qualitative direction question keyed to the source-supported glide path. Source: NISM Series XVII, June 2025, p.111-116, 160.
